The grass-topped dirt cliff shoulders at the left and right edges also show a top. The cobble in rows 16-31 reads as ground or landing. The view matches a south-facing cliff with steps cut through it, and no isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small 3x1-tile stair strip: a grass lip on top, two horizontal stone step bands, and wood posts at the sides. Measured facts are comparable to the references: 6 visible tones per tile (paving 7, grass 3), 0% near-flat coverage, and 14 distinct colours in total. By eye it is plainly simpler than the paving reference, which has cobbles shaded one by one with highlights and mortar lines. The candidate's step faces are mostly smooth bands of about 3 grey tones, with only a light top edge and a dark underside. They have no per-stone grain, speckle or clump variation, so the shading ramp is shallow at about 3 steps against 5-6. The 41% near-neutral dark edge pixels point to a partly neutral outline. The paving reference is 80% neutral on this measure, but the candidate's dark lines still read as a generic grey-black on the steps rather than a clearly tinted dark material tone. Taken together the piece looks flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails with the benefit of the doubt withheld.
